subject: Biology
title: Meiosis: Shuffling the Deck
description: A short lesson to help you apply Meiosis: Shuffling the Deck.

hook.text: Meiosis makes sex cells with half the chromosomes—23 instead of 46 in humans.

buildup.text: Two rounds of division turn one cell into four genetically unique cells.

discovery.text: Crossing over swaps segments between chromosomes, creating new combinations.

twist.text: Without meiosis, every child would be a clone. Genetic variation would vanish.

climax.text: When sperm meets egg, two half-sets unite into a full genome—a new individual.

punchline.text: Meiosis makes everyone one of a kind.

quiz.question: How many cells does meiosis produce from one starting cell?

details.summary: Meiosis is the specialized cell division that produces gametes with half the chromosome number. It shuffles genetic material through crossing over and independent assortment, ensuring that each egg or sperm is genetically unique and different from every other.
details.whyItMatters: Meiosis generates the genetic diversity that drives evolution and makes every individual unique. Errors in meiosis cause chromosomal disorders like Down syndrome and are a leading cause of miscarriage.
takeaways: Meiosis halves chromosome number from 46 to 23 in human gametes
Crossing over swaps DNA segments between homologous chromosomes
Independent assortment creates over 8 million possible chromosome combinations

faq.question: How does meiosis differ from mitosis?
faq.answer: Mitosis produces two identical cells with the full chromosome set for growth and repair. Meiosis produces four genetically unique cells with half the chromosomes for reproduction. Meiosis involves two divisions and includes crossing over for genetic shuffling.

faq.question: What causes Down syndrome in relation to meiosis?
faq.answer: Down syndrome results from nondisjunction during meiosis, where chromosome 21 fails to separate properly. This produces a gamete with two copies instead of one, resulting in three copies of chromosome 21 in the offspring, called trisomy 21.
